answers.text:
The two maps is about the village Ferndale in the year 1985 and how it is in 2020.

Firstly, in 1985 there is a big farmland in the north part of the village, on the top of the main road. But in 2020 this farmland is not exist any more, because they build there a housing estate with many small house and street.

Secondly, the school is in the south west and it is a small building in 1985. In 2020 the school become more bigger, the building take more place than before.

Thirdly, in the east side there is a shop near the road. In 2020 this small shop is change to a supermarket and next to the supermarket they make a car park for the car of the customer.

Also the main road is more wide in 2020 and on the river there is a new bridge for the people who walk. So the life of the resident become more comfortable now, because they find everything near the home.

why_this_band.task_response: Four of the five changes (farmland, school, shop, road and bridge) are given in sequence, but a sentence stating the overview of the map as a whole is nowhere to be found, and the unchanged forest and houses are never mentioned. The final paragraph adds a comment that is not in the map (life became more comfortable, they don't go to town to shop).
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The Firstly / Secondly / Thirdly pattern carries only the sequence, not the logic of the paragraphs. Even so, the reader does not lose the thread because each paragraph deals with a single change.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Location language is limited to big, north part, east side, near the road; items such as opposite, to the east of are missing. Forms like more bigger, take more place, more wide slow the reader down.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Almost every sentence has an error: maps is, is not exist, they build there, is change, more bigger, the car of the customer. The whole text is written in the present tense although 1985 is the past; structures are almost entirely simple sentences.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Drop the comment in the final paragraph and replace it with an overview that compares the two maps in one sentence (a rural settlement turns into a dense one), and convert the 1985 section into the past tense.

answers.text:
The two maps show the changes which happened in the village of Ferndale between 1985 and 2020.

Overall, the village became much more built up during this period: the farmland in the north was replaced by houses, and the services for the residents were made larger, while the natural features were mostly kept.

In 1985 the whole area to the north of the main road was a farmland. By 2020 this space has been completely covered by a housing estate, which is divided by several small streets. This is the biggest change between the two maps. The woodland in the north east corner, however, stayed exactly the same in the both maps.

There were also changes in the south of the village. The school, which is situated in the south west, was enlarged and now it occupies a bigger area than before. On the eastern side of the road, the small shop disappeared and a supermarket with a car park was built there.

Finally, the main road was widened and a new footbridge was constructed over the river, so the people can cross the water on foot. The row of the houses along the road did not change.

why_this_band.task_response: The overview is clearly present in the second paragraph, and all five changes are given, including the unchanged forest and houses. How much the school and the estate grew is left unmeasured, and the changes are not ranked by size.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: Paragraphs are logically split: overview, north, south, the remaining two changes. Links are accurate but do not go beyond familiar patterns like There were also changes / Finally.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Task-appropriate items such as built up, housing estate, enlarged, widened, footbridge are present. In the both maps and was a farmland do not quite settle as forms.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Relative clauses and the passive are correctly formed, and long sentences do not fall apart. Half the sentences have an article or tense error (a farmland, has been completely covered, in the both maps, which is situated, the people can cross, the row of the houses); meaning is never blocked.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Instead of listing the changes in equal order, rank them by size — the complete disappearance of the farmland first, then the rest — and describe the school's expansion by its direction.

answers.text:
The two maps illustrate how the village of Ferndale changed over the thirty-five years between 1985 and 2020.

Overall, what had been a largely rural settlement became a considerably denser one: the open land north of the main road was given over to housing, the existing services were expanded to match, and only the woodland and the older houses were left untouched.

The most striking change took place in the northern half of the village. In 1985 this area consisted of a single stretch of farmland running west from the woodland. By 2020 the fields had disappeared entirely beneath a housing estate laid out on a grid of streets, which occupies the whole of the space the farm once did. The woodland in the north-eastern corner, by contrast, survived the period intact.

South of the road the pattern is one of expansion rather than replacement. The school remained on its original site but was enlarged, extending both eastwards and southwards, while the modest shop to the east of the road gave way to a supermarket with its own car park alongside it.

Two smaller alterations complete the picture. The main road itself was widened, and a footbridge was thrown across the river at the southern edge of the village, where in 1985 there had been no crossing at all. The houses lining the road between the school and the river are shown unchanged on both maps.

why_this_band.task_response: The overview states both the direction of the transformation and what stayed the same. Every change is given together with its location, and change versus expansion are named as two separate patterns; comment never enters anywhere.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: Information is grouped not item by item but as north/south and major/minor change. Items such as by contrast and rather than replacement build the link through the sentence's own work.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Less common items such as given over to housing, laid out on a grid of streets, gave way to, survived the period intact appear with the right collocation. Directional language is consistent and natural.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: The past perfect, a participle-headed structure, a relative clause and a where clause of place rotate under control. Errors are rare; thrown across the river is slightly heavy but does not stop the reader.

answers.what_would_lift_it: At this level, progress is about measure rather than detail: comparing the area covered by the estate proportionally with the former farmland would make the text one step more precise.
